classification.difficultyReason: Interpret successive constant and variable rates in a real-world graph and infer school break times.

content.prompt: The graph shows the number of cans of soft drink in the vending machine of a school.

spec.description: Qualitative time graph with half-hour grid lines, hourly time labels, no numerical can-count scale and a positive minimum. The final flattening decrease continues slightly beyond 4 pm. Drawing coordinates express relative levels only.
spec.mathematics: Constant from 8–10 am; decreasing at a decreasing rate from 10–10:30 am; constant-rate increase to 11 am; constant to 12:30 pm; constant-rate decrease to 1:30 pm; constant-rate increase to 2 pm; constant to 3 pm; decreasing at a decreasing rate thereafter.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph and labels are permanent student givens; supplied prose answers are excluded.

children.label: a
children.prompt: When do you think the recess and lunch breaks occur in this school?

answer.worked: Recess is likely to begin at 10 am and lunch at 12:30 pm, when the number of cans starts to decrease as students buy drinks.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Describe in words how the number of cans varies during the day.

answer.short: The number stays constant until 10 am, then decreases at a decreasing rate until 10:30 am. It increases at a constant rate until 11 am, stays constant until 12:30 pm, decreases at a constant rate until 1:30 pm, then increases at a constant rate until 2 pm. It stays constant until 3 pm, then decreases at a decreasing rate through 4 pm and slightly beyond.
answer.worked:
From 8 am to 10 am, the horizontal graph shows a constant number of cans. From 10 am to 10:30 am, cans are sold and the number decreases at a decreasing rate as the curve becomes less steep.

From 10:30 am to 11 am, the machine is refilled at a constant rate. The number then stays constant until 12:30 pm.

From 12:30 pm to 1:30 pm, the number decreases at a constant rate. From 1:30 pm to 2 pm, the machine is refilled at a constant rate. The number stays constant from 2 pm to 3 pm.

From 3 pm through 4 pm and slightly beyond, the number decreases at a decreasing rate: the downward curve becomes progressively flatter.
